strands.title: Form and perspective
strands.summary: Lines, ellipses, boxes, perspective and construction: the tools for building any object in 3D on paper. Most of the Drawabox order lives here, from line control to everyday objects and vehicles.

strands.title: Observation, figure and head
strands.summary: Looking, measuring and checking against the real thing: contour, sighting, still life, gesture, the figure, the head and light seen from life. This strand trains accuracy and fills the visual library.

strands.title: Invention and design
strands.summary: Drawing from imagination on purpose: prompts, memory, invented objects, figures and creatures, composition, characters and places. It runs from week one and always ends with a check against reference.

phases.title: Start drawing
phases.summary: A minimal kit, posture and a five-minute warm-up, a practice method built on short sessions and memory redraws, and a baseline set of ten drawings from imagination that you repeat at every benchmark. Most of it fits in the first two weeks.

phases.title: Line, form and looking
phases.summary: Confident lines and freehand ellipses, simple volumes with overlap and cross-contours, contour drawing, gesture, memory drawing and the play strand. The gesture ladder, memory redraws and invention prompts start here and continue as ongoing practice.

phases.title: Boxes, measuring and first inventions
phases.summary: Boxes in perspective and the freehand box challenge, measuring by eye, block-in, still life from life and ways to check a drawing. Value and composition arrive early, and you start inventing objects from boxes and cylinders.

phases.title: Perspective and construction
phases.summary: Horizon and vanishing points, one- and two-point perspective, ellipses and cylinders in perspective, organic forms with contour lines, and construction from primitives. You apply it to everyday objects and to objects you rotate and redesign from imagination.

phases.title: Figure and head
phases.summary: Figure construction and proportion, mannequin figures from imagination, the constructed head, features and expression, hands, drapery and shape language. Anatomy, foreshortening, dynamic poses and portrait likeness are deepening modules you can take later.

phases.title: Light, value and form
phases.summary: How light falls on simple forms, shading techniques in graphite and pen, and shading things you invented. Edges, light types, cast shadows, materials and a rendered still life follow as deepening work.

phases.title: Animals, nature and machines
phases.summary: Construction applied to plants, insects, birds, reptiles and mammals, then animal movement and machines, in the order Drawabox teaches them. Mammal construction is the spine module; the rest deepen it.

phases.title: Places and stories
phases.summary: Building invented environments and telling a story in a picture, then landscape, architecture, location sketching and a perspective scene capstone.

phases.title: Characters, creatures and finished pieces
phases.summary: Character and creature design from a brief, then costume, acting, stylisation, harder figures from imagination, style and a full visual development workflow.

phases.title: Colour and media
phases.summary: A branch that opens once value and light on form are in place: colour theory, mixing, colour in light and shadow, mood, digital painting, inking, finishing and an optional media sampler. Paper first; digital is optional.

short_session.description: Warm-up plus one revisit. Three minutes of the current warm-up drill (lines, ellipses, boxes or 30-second gestures), then one due revisit drawn cold with the lesson closed and checked against its listed checks. Use it on tired days and training evenings; it counts as a session.

hours_note: Gate hours (est_hours) cover the lesson and the drills needed to pass the module's checks. Ongoing hours (ongoing_hours) are practice that continues after passing, such as the box challenge, the gesture ladder, memory redraws and invention play, spread over months and not added to path totals. All hours are estimates by the research passes, not measurements.

evidence_labels.opened: A research pass opened the page and the link resolved. Cost and contents may still be only partly confirmed; read free_notes.
evidence_labels.search-result: Seen only in search-result summaries on 2026-10-13. The page itself was not opened. Treat as unverified.
evidence_labels.unchecked: Not checked by the second pass; the first pass could not confirm it either. Treat as unverified.

link_meaning_extra.unchecked: the current address has not been link-checked (new entry, or an address fixed from search results)

known_gaps: Drawabox could not be opened by any research pass. Its lessons and challenges were confirmed only through search results, so every Drawabox entry stays unverified. Open drawabox.com yourself before relying on one.

Most second-round evidence (link fixes, the 28 new resources, the Drawabox lesson map) comes from search-result summaries, not opened pages. Those entries carry evidence search-result and verified false.

Verified means a research pass opened the page and the link resolved. It does not always mean cost and contents were both confirmed: 23 verified entries say in their own notes that part of the claim was not seen.
Proko entries that point at one lesson but are labelled part free were not resolved; a single video is either free to watch or Premium. Check the lesson page before planning around it.
No free public live figure-drawing session was found to replace the New Masters Academy Friday session, which now needs a subscription. Timed photo tools in the library cover the gesture practice.

Still thin after the second pass: memory drawing, curvilinear perspective, portrait likeness, reptiles and fish, ships and aircraft, ornament, rocks, fire and smoke, costume and props, cartooning, foreshortening of objects, charcoal handling, and turnarounds or model sheets. Original lesson notes cover these where they sit in the plan.

Bargue plates are linked through Wikimedia Commons and Rijksmuseum single-plate files. The Internet Archive Bargue uploads are scans of the modern ACR Edition book with copyrighted commentary and are not linked.
Loomis and Nicolaides are not linked because no legitimate free copy was found. Harold Speed's books stay in copyright in Australia until 1 January 2028, so they are not linked either.
Reddit communities and several university course pages could not be opened, so their current state is unknown. Non-English and animation-studio sources were not researched.
Hours are estimates, not measurements. Recalibrate them from your own session logs after the first two months.
Benchmark tasks, tolerances and each chapter's checks were written for this curriculum from syllabus criteria and the research notes, not taken from a published standard.

The practice loop (revisits, retrieval, interleaving, feedback) rests on general learning research; no study found tested these methods on drawing. Revisit intervals and timer defaults are design choices to tune.
Prices are as displayed on 2026-10-13 and change.
